newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S HORN SAYS GDP GROWTH COULD REACH FOUR OR FIVE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S HORN SAYS GDP GROWTH COULD REACH FOUR OR FIVE.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn said om Monday Hungary would reach four to five percent economic growth from 1998.
"Foreigners say Hungary is the only country in the region which in the coming years will have an economic growth which is sustainable," Horn told reporters.
"But what I consider very important is that they say from 1998 we can have four to five percent growth."
Hungary saw GDP growth of 1.0 percent in 1996 and the finance ministry is predicting a two to three percent increase this year.
At a monthly media briefing Horn said Hungary was further along the path of budget reform to stabilise its economy than other countries in the region.

"As regards the macrofinancial indicators, as a result of stabilisation...only Hungary is characterised by a reform of the public sphere, that is education, health and the organisation of the administration.
"Such large-scale programmes have not begun or have only partly begun in the other central European countries," he said.
